extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning. The task is multiple choice question answering: given a question and two possible solutions, a model or a human must choose the most appropriate solution.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Bras, R. L., Gao, J., & Choi, Y. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. AAAI.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com. They were asked to glance at the instructions, pull out or construct two component tasks, articulate the goal (often centered on atypical materials), and how to achieve it. They also provided a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid (a trick).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm, which discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples with low agreement were removed during validation. The AFLite algorithm was used to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were provided a prompt derived from instructables.com. They articulated a goal and a valid solution, then provided a 'trick' (a permutation of the solution that makes it invalid). Qualification HITs were run prior to the main stage and validation HITs afterwards.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed. Human performance was calculated by a majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias swamped the dataset when using unconstrained prompts (people drawn to prototypical solutions). Stylistic artifacts and trivial examples were present and removed using AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Large pretrained models struggle (77% accuracy vs 95% human). Reporting bias limits data. Examples requiring expert level knowledge were removed. Automated methods trained on large web crawls may eventually surpass human performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding, Training, Testing, Validation
